purpose: RF-SP-SCORE-HARDENING-1 evidence snapshot for a future SP-CLEANUP-01 phase — files whose sp_total_score would regress against audit/salad_score_baseline.json if metricLocNormalized (max(raw LOC, logical statements)) replaced the raw-LOC-only metric in the real scoring pipeline. Report-only today: this file is NOT read by run_salad_score.mjs, the ratchet, or any score calculation.
method: Measured in isolation (isolated impact script, not wired into runSaladScore's scoreFile/scoreRepo), then each flagged file was read directly to classify the cause with evidence — never assumed.

classificationLegend.deuda_vieja: Real pre-existing dense code — multiple genuine statements were already fused per physical line since the file's original authorship, not compacted afterward from a more readable version to game the score.
classificationLegend.gaming_reciente: Code that was demonstrably more readable before and was recently compacted to lower its measured score.
classificationLegend.falso_positivo: The metric flags it but the pattern is not actually a problem (e.g. a legitimate single-expression facade).

candidates.evidence: Every alignLeft/Right/Top/Bottom/Center method fuses an if/else branch + DS.saveHistory() call onto one physical line (e.g. L4: "alignLeft() { if (typeof CommandEngine !== 'undefined') CommandEngine.alignLefts?.(); else this._fallback('left'); DS.saveHistory(); }"). Confirmed via direct read — this is the file's original authored style (subsystem SS-36 'alignment-runtime', historical P17E refactor per architecture/ownership-map.json notes), not a recent compaction.

_ensureState() fuses a let + try/catch + 2 assignments + a method call + a return onto one physical line. Every other method (getState, isEnabled, setEnabled, setChannel) follows the same dense one-line-per-method style throughout the whole file. Confirmed via direct read.

_isDebugConsoleCall/_installConsoleGate/_handleHomeClick/init all fuse multiple if-statements, assignments, and calls onto single physical lines. Same dense native style as DebugTrace.js (the two files are companions). Confirmed via direct read.

Small delta — a handful of lines with 2-3 real statements each (declare + configure pattern). Same established dense style as the rest of this codebase's engine files, not a recent compaction. Did not cause a baseline regression at the time of this measurement.

L48 alone is 926 characters: the mkCol() helper builds ~4 DOM elements, assigns ~10 style/content properties, and wires 2 event handlers, all on one physical line. This density is the file's original authored style (confirmed via direct read of the surrounding lines, all similarly dense: L57, L61, L62, L67-69 all exceed 250 characters) — not something compacted down from a more readable prior version.

A hand-written formula tokenizer/parser (Crystal-like expressions) with a deliberately compact native style throughout: e.g. "const tok=[]; let i=0,n=src.length;" and "if(/\s/.test(src[i])){i++;continue;}" — many real statements per line since this file's original authorship. Confirmed via direct read.

Follows the SAME 'create element; set property;' one-line-per-widget style already established since Fase 13 (this repo's UDS 4.1 epic) and shared by sibling dialog files (SqlCommandEditor.js, StoredProcedurePicker.js) since Fase 8/11 — a project-wide established convention for compact dialog construction, not something introduced to lower this specific file's score. Did not cause a baseline regression at the time of this measurement.

excludedByDesign.engines/SelectionEngine.js: Initially flagged by an EARLIER, less precise version of countLogicalStatements (a facade method like 'm() { return Other.m(this, args); }' was incorrectly counted as a 2-unit block regardless of its single statement). Fixed: a function-kind block only adds its +2 when it wraps MORE THAN ONE real statement; a control-kind block (if/for/while/etc.) always does, since control flow is conventionally always multi-line. Re-measured after the fix: no longer flagged. Kept here as a documented false-positive precedent, not a cleanup candidate.

marginClassificationLegend.note: Revised 2026-07-09. floor(limit * 0.90) applied blindly is correct for large-cap metrics (LOC, normalized LOC, bytes) but too noisy for small integer sp_total_score values — at baseline=11 it demanded target<=9, i.e. a 2-point drop, when a genuine 1-point improvement is already meaningful. Replaced with a tiered rule keyed to baseline magnitude for sp_total_score specifically; large-cap metrics keep the original floor(limit*0.90) rule unchanged.

largeMetricRule.appliesTo: LOC, normalized LOC, byte counts, and any other high-cap raw metric — NOT sp_total_score.

marginClassificationLegend.STRUCTURAL_WARNING: Applies only within a WARNING band per the rule above matching the metric type, AND all of: ratchet passes (current <= baseline); no regression; the LOC-normalization concern is already resolved for this file (RF-SP-SCORE-HARDENING-1 / SP-HARDENING-NESTING-01 applied); a real compensating improvement or genuine cleanup was already made; further reduction would require artificial compaction, artificial abstraction, breaking the shared architectural pattern, or a behavior change; and explicit line-level evidence is recorded.
marginClassificationLegend.FAIL: sp_total_score > baseline — a real ratchet regression.
marginClassificationLegend.BLOCKED: A real refactor attempt was measured and rejected before touching the real file, because it would cause a FAIL (score > baseline) with no further real compensating reduction available.
marginClassificationLegend.DEFERRED_NO_CLEAN_GAIN: The file has no registered baseline (so the ratchet cannot fail on it), but a full reformat-to-readable measured no compensating drop in any real metric (complexity/nesting/responsibilities/globals/topLevelSideEffects all stayed identical) — only loc rose. Per explicit user rule, absence of a baseline is never used as license to raise a score with no real gain. Left untouched.
